provenance.purpose: Classify each item a real `R CMD check --as-cran` run reports as either a package DEFECT or an artefact of the MEASURING ENVIRONMENT. The item names, counts and verbatim text are read from the check log by tools/status/facts.R; only the classification and the source attribution below are editorial.
provenance.check_command: R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz
provenance.environment_note: _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false was required because 10 Suggests are not installable in this environment. qpdf is absent; HTML Tidy is older than R expects.

items.summary: CRAN reports this as a New submission -- the package has never been on CRAN -- and flags 2 URLs that redirect 301.
items.source: README.md (https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/edaphos needs a trailing slash) and inst/doc/case-cerrado-end-to-end.html (https://github.com/ipeaGIT/geobr moved to https://github.com/ipea/geobr). Tarball is 15734027 bytes.
items.fix: Add the trailing slash in README.md and update the geobr URL in vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd. The 'New submission' line is not fixable and not a defect in itself -- it is recorded here because it contradicts every artefact that implies the package is released.
items.note: 'New submission' is R's own confirmation that nothing named edaphos exists on CRAN, at version 3.10.0 with 43 NEWS releases behind it.

items.fix: See findings FC68E1D (move .moco_require_torch below the argument validation in R/foundation_weights.R) and FAEC54C (validate num.trees in R/active_fit.R, seed the test).

items.summary: pdflatex cannot typeset two raw Unicode characters used in Rd text.
items.source: R/foundation_finetune.R:165 (U+2265 GREATER-THAN OR EQUAL) and R/foundation_finetune.R:436 (U+2208 ELEMENT OF); man/*.Rd is roxygen-generated so the fix must land in R/ and be re-documented.
items.fix: Replace with \eqn{\ge} / \eqn{\in} or ASCII, then roxygen2::roxygenise(). The 165 em-dashes and 18 en-dashes in Rd are safe -- R's Rd-to-LaTeX pass maps them.

items.check: checking PDF version of manual without index
items.summary: Same root cause as the PDF-manual WARNING.
Escaped LaTeX special \~ in Rd text.
Installed size far above the CRAN 5 MB guidance; becomes a NOTE on CRAN's incoming checks.
items.fix: See finding FDE7C43. The single cheapest win is re-encoding man/figures/logo.png.

items.check: checking for hidden files and directories
items.summary: .git was included in the tarball because .Rbuildignore has no ^\.git$ entry.
items.fix: Add ^\.git$. Note this surfaces here because the build ran from a git worktree, where .git is a plain file rather than a directory; adding the pattern makes the build correct from either layout.

items.summary: GATEOUT.rds at top level -- a byproduct of the audit tooling, not of the package.
items.source: removed from the worktree before the clean baseline run
items.fix: None. Absent from the clean baseline.

items.summary: The local HTML Tidy is older than R requires, so HTML validation was skipped.

items.check: checking for non-standard things in the check directory
items.summary: edaphos-manual.tex left behind by the failed LaTeX run.
items.source: consequence of the PDF-manual failure above
items.fix: Disappears once the Unicode fix lands.

items.check: checking for detritus in the temp directory
items.summary: Temporary directory left by the failed LaTeX run.
items.source: consequence of the PDF-manual failure above
items.fix: Disappears once the Unicode fix lands.

items.summary: The tarball cannot be built at all when the Suggests package dagitty is absent: the vignette's setup chunk calls causal_cerrado_dag() with no availability guard, so build aborts. DESCRIPTION claims 'A synthesised Cerrado dataset is bundled so every vignette runs offline'.
items.fix: Guard the chunk with requireNamespace('dagitty') (the pattern the R/ code already uses via .causal_require_dagitty), or set eval=FALSE with a precomputed result, as the other heavy vignettes do.
items.note: CRAN installs Suggests, so this would not block CRAN itself -- but it does block every contributor and any reproduction attempt on a lean machine, and it falsifies the offline claim.
